paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: real love for people looks like showing up for them. Paul says of Timothy, "I have nobody else like him who will genuinely care for your needs." (Philippians 2:20) Then he says that all the others "look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ." (Philippians 2:21) Caring about people's actual needs is rare, and it's one of the ways we look after what matters to Jesus.

Now look at Epaphroditus. He was sick, nearly unto death, and Paul says he was distressed because the Philippians had heard about it (Philippians 2:26, 27). I think that's a man whose mind was on the people he served, not on himself. Paul says he nearly died for the work of Christ, "risking his life" for others (Philippians 2:30). That's the kind of service that costs something, and I'm telling you, it matters to God and to the people around us.

So Paul says to welcome men like him in the Lord with great joy and to honor them (Philippians 2:29). Friend, that's your job too: notice the people who serve quietly and thank them out loud. And ask yourself who needs you to show up this week, because that's where the cookies get made. You don't have to be famous to do it. You just have to care.
